item.question: Why should the extension of the vertical and horizontal sides of the original square pass through the vertices of the dotted square?
steps: The diagonal of the original square makes 45° with each side of the original square.
At an end of the diagonal, the dotted square has a 90° corner.
The side of the original square at that end makes 45° with the diagonal, so it splits the 90° corner into 45° and 45°: it bisects the angle of the dotted square.
In a square, the line that bisects an angle is a diagonal, and it passes through the opposite vertex.

concept_name: Why is the folded shape PQRS a square, and how much paper is it?

item.question: Fold the corners inward so the creases pass through the midpoints of the sides. Why is PQRS a square, and why is its area half that of the original paper?
steps: P, Q, R and S are the midpoints of the sides of the paper.
Join QS and PR: they cross at the centre of the paper at right angles.
The four triangles around the centre, such as the one with vertices P, Q and the centre, each have two sides equal to half the side of the paper and a right angle between them, so they are congruent.
So PQ = QR = RS = SP.
Each of these right triangles has two equal sides, so its other two angles are 45° each; each angle of PQRS, such as angle SPQ, is 45° + 45°, a right angle.
Four equal sides and four right angles: PQRS is a square.
Each folded corner is congruent to the triangle it covers, so the paper is 8 triangles and PQRS is 4 of them: half.
item.answer: PQRS has four equal sides and four right angles, so it is a square; it is 4 of the paper's 8 congruent triangles, so it has half the area

concept_name: Can root two be written as a fraction m over n?

item.question: Can √2 be expressed as a fraction m/n, where m and n are counting numbers?
steps: Suppose √2 = m/n.
Square both sides: 2 = m²/n², so 2n² = m².
In m², the prime 2 occurs an even number of times.
In n² the prime 2 occurs an even number of times, so in 2n² it occurs an odd number of times.
One number cannot hold the prime 2 both an even and an odd number of times.
So the supposition is impossible.
item.answer: No: √2 is not a fraction m/n (Euclid, Elements); √2 = 1.41421356... goes on forever

steps: The square on the hypotenuse is made of T, U and V.
The two given squares, joined, are made of V, W and X.
T, U, W and X are congruent, so T and U together have the same area as W and X together.

item.question: Explain why all the angles of this new 4-sided figure are right angles and so it is a square.
steps: In the right triangle with sides a and b, call one acute angle x; the angles add to 180 and one is 90, so the other acute angle is 90 − x.
At the corner on the bottom edge, the angle x of W and the angle 90 − x of X lie on the straight edge on either side of the corner, so the corner is 180 − x − (90 − x), which is 90.
At each of the other three corners, an angle x and an angle 90 − x together make the corner: x + (90 − x), which is 90.
Four equal sides and four right angles make a square.

item.question: State Baudhāyana's theorem on right-angled triangles, and say why it has two names.
steps: Take a right triangle with shorter sides a and b.
The side opposite the right angle is the hypotenuse, c.
The squares on a and b, cut and rearranged, exactly cover the square on c.
So a² + b² = c².
Baudhāyana (c. 800 BCE) stated it first in general form; Pythagoras (c. 500 BCE) studied it a couple of hundred years later.
item.answer: If a right-angled triangle has sides a, b and hypotenuse c, then a² + b² = c²

item.question: A lotus tip is 1 unit above the water. Swayed by the breeze, the tip touches the water 3 units from its original position. Find the depth of the lake.
steps_tex: Let the depth be $x$; the stem has length $x + 1$.
The upright stem is perpendicular to the water, so there is a right angle at the water surface.
The bent stem, of length $x + 1$, is the hypotenuse; the other sides are $x$ and $3$.
Subtract $x^2$ from both sides: $9 = 2x + 1$.
item.answer_tex: The lake is $4\text{ units}$ deep

item.answer: The lake is 4 units deep
item.text:
$1$. Let the depth be $x$; the stem has length $x + 1$.
$2$. The upright stem is perpendicular to the water, so there is a right angle at the water surface.
$3$. The bent stem, of length $x + 1$, is the hypotenuse; the other sides are $x$ and $3$.

$7$. $2x = 8$, so $x = 4$.
Answer: The lake is $4\text{ units}$ deep

item.question: Find the Colours! Three boxes hold only red, only blue and only green balls. Every label (RED, BLUE, GREEN) is wrong. Open one box only. How do you fix the labels?
steps: No label is correct, so each box has a wrong label.
Open the box labelled RED and take out one ball; it is blue or green, never red.
Say it is blue: that box is BLUE.
The box labelled GREEN cannot hold green (its label is wrong) and cannot hold blue (already found), so it holds red.
The box labelled BLUE then holds green.
If the ball is green instead, the box labelled RED is GREEN, the box labelled BLUE holds red and the box labelled GREEN holds blue.
item.answer: Open any one box, for example the one labelled RED; the colour seen and the fact that every label is wrong fix all three labels
